official.deadline_note: Platform-published application window for international and resident students: 16 September 2026 to 6 October 2026 for the Second Semester Academic Calendar 2026. No separate institutional deadline is published; admission is decided by the chosen educational institution.
official.status_note: The Study in Saudi homepage publishes the Second Semester Academic Calendar 2026 timeline: start of the application period for international and resident students on 16 September 2026 and end on 6 October 2026. As verified on 10 October 2026 that window has closed and no later cycle is published on the platform.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full Scholarships tier: 'Tuition, housing & living - all covered'. Institution programme listings describe a Full Scholarship as 'The sponsoring entity covers all scholarship costs; the student bears no financial burden', and the full-scholarship programme pages list 'Tuition Waiver' first among the included benefits.
benefits: Full Scholarships: 'Tuition, housing & living - all covered'
eligibility: Applicant must be 16 years of age or older
A valid passport with at least 6 months validity from the intended date of entry to the Kingdom
Acceptance from a licensed and accredited educational institution in the Kingdom
Proof of financial ability to cover tuition and living expenses, or a financial guarantee
For the long-term visa: a medical report confirming freedom from infectious diseases, and a medical insurance document for the visa holder and dependants
Proof of proficiency in the language of study, except for those wishing to study Arabic; written consent of the guardian and companions for visa holders under 18 years of age
requirements: Apply for the scholarship through the educational institution where you wish to study by submitting an admission application; the institution reviews the application and issues an admission decision, after which the institution and the Ministry of Education complete the final admission procedures
Complete your platform profile before applying to academic programs
Attested certificates and required documents per the educational institution's requirements
A student cannot receive two scholarships for the same academic degree
Programme-level required attachments (for example a High School Diploma on the listed bachelor programmes) must be uploaded to the profile
documents: Valid passport with at least 6 months validity
Acceptance from a licensed and accredited educational institution in the Kingdom
Proof of proficiency in the language of study (unless studying Arabic)
Medical report confirming freedom from infectious diseases (long-term visa)
Medical insurance document for the visa holder and dependants (long-term visa)
High School Diploma (required attachment on the listed bachelor programmes)
selection_criteria: No selection criteria or weighting are published; the chosen educational institution reviews the application and issues an admission decision
The platform states an application is rejected where one or more of the admission requirements for the programme or educational institution were not met
Aptitude or achievement test scores are retrieved into the account through the 'Update Data' button in the personal profile
coverage: Living costs: accommodation and a monthly stipend
application_method: Create a profile on the Study in Saudi platform and complete it
Browse the participating institutions and programmes, filtering by degree, language, city and scholarship type
Submit an admission application to the chosen educational institution through the platform
Await the institution's admission decision, then the Ministry of Education's final admission processing
official.application_route: Apply through the Ministry of Education's Study in Saudi platform (studyinsaudi.sa) by submitting an admission application to the chosen institution; there is no separate central scholarship form.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is published; the platform's application windows are for 'international and resident students', and each programme listing is tagged with a student type of International or Resident.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. The platform is designed for international students and researchers, and programme listings include an 'International' student type alongside 'Resident'.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject or sponsoring-agency restriction is published; programme listings state the language of instruction, gender and student type (International/Resident) per programme.
official.duration: Programme-dependent: the platform publishes a duration per programme (4 years on the listed Jouf University bachelor tracks, 2 years for listed master's programmes and 3 years for listed PhD programmes). The long-term study visa it supports is issued for 1 year and is renewable annually.
official.description: The Ministry of Education of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia operates the Study in Saudi platform, which administers educational scholarships for international and resident students at Saudi universities. Its Study Visa & Pathways page sets out three pathways: Full Scholarships, described as 'Tuition, housing & living - all covered'; Partial Scholarships, described as partial support; and Paid Study Programs, which are self-funded. Scholarships are applied for through the educational institution where the student wishes to study, which reviews the application and issues an admission decision before the Ministry of Education completes final admission procedures.
official.english_requirement: No English test or score threshold is published. For the long-term study visa the platform requires 'proof of proficiency in the language of study, except for those wishing to study Arabic'; for Arabic-medium study it promotes the Hamza Arabic proficiency test for non-native speakers (King Salman Global Academy for Arabic Language).

verification.notes: Checked the Ministry of Education's Study in Saudi platform directly: the Study Visa & Pathways page (tier wording and visa eligibility), the programme directory and two full-scholarship programme detail pages (included benefits list), the FAQ, an institution page (full-scholarship wording) and the homepage timeline. The platform publishes no monetary value for the scholarship award: the figure shown on full-scholarship programme pages is a struck-through pre-discount tuition price with no currency or period label, so funding_amount, funding_currency and funding_period remain null.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a stand-alone scholarship form: you submit an admission application to a specific programme at a Saudi university through the Study in Saudi platform, and a Full Scholarship is awarded through that institutional admission decision. The published package for the Full Scholarships tier is a tuition waiver, a monthly stipend, university accommodation, medical insurance and travel tickets, so the cost of attendance is not the usual risk. The binding constraints are timing and programme fit: the platform's published window for the Second Semester Academic Calendar 2026 ran 16 September to 6 October 2026, and only programmes tagged 'Full Scholarship' and matched to your student type (International or Resident) are actually open to you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International and resident applicants aged 16 or over who hold, or are completing, a school-leaving or degree qualification that meets a listed Saudi university's own admission requirements and who want tuition, housing and living costs covered.
application_readiness_checklist: Complete the platform profile first - it must be finished before any programme application can be submitted
Filter the programme directory by Scholarship Type = Full Scholarship and by Student Type (International or Resident) before investing time in an application
Prepare the programme's required attachment (for example a High School Diploma on bachelor tracks) and upload it to the profile so it can be reused across applications
Hold a passport with at least six months' validity from your intended entry date, since the passport number cannot be changed after submission
Check the chosen institution's own admissions page for attested-certificate and language requirements before the platform window opens
Have the medical report and medical insurance arrangements ready for the long-term visa stage
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme tagged Partial Scholarship or Paid Study while assuming full funding - those tiers leave part or all of the tuition with the student
Failing the long-term visa conditions: under-six-month passport validity, missing medical report or missing medical insurance for the holder and dependants
Not meeting the institution's own admission requirements, which the platform names as the reason applications are rejected
Gender and student-type restrictions printed on the programme card (for example Male/Female and International/Resident)
Applying while already holding a scholarship for the same academic degree, which the platform blocks
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Once a Full Scholarship is awarded the platform states the student bears no financial burden; before and around that, applicants still fund their own document attestation and translation, the visa-stage proof of funds or financial guarantee, medical insurance and travel arrangements for dependants not covered by the award, and consular or travel costs - the platform publishes no figures for any of these.
document_audit: Passport number, residency number, Gulf ID, gender and nationality cannot be edited after registration; only contact details and qualification data can be updated later
Application data other than contact information cannot be modified after submission, so errors must be caught before submitting
Certificates must be attested and meet the individual institution's document requirements, which vary by university
Programme attachments such as the High School Diploma are stored on the profile; a missing attachment blocks the application
Aptitude or achievement test scores must be pulled into the account with 'Update Data' if they do not appear automatically
alerts: Timing: the published Second Semester Academic Calendar 2026 window (16 September to 6 October 2026) has closed and no next-cycle dates are published - re-check the homepage before planning
There is no separate central scholarship deadline: the institution's admission decision sits between you and the award
An application can only be cancelled while the institution has taken no action on it
An 'Under Process' status means the institution is still reviewing; the decision is not immediate and the status must be monitored on the platform
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the admission application on the platform, the chosen institution reviews and issues its admission decision, the institution and the Ministry of Education then complete final admission procedures, and the student proceeds to study visa issuance.
